- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), then corrects downward — suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized: model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert toward lower levels after peaks.
- Forecast bias is upward: model starts above true outcome by 1–3 points on average, especially in the first 10 days.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window — often underestimates sharp drops.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts remain elevated even when true price is trending down.
